name: BlockSwapWrapperGolemNetworkToken
title: The Unclaimed Wrapper of Spurious Dragon
tagline: A lonely token born in March remains haunted by an owner who was never named.

chapters.heading: The birth of the wrapped token
paragraphs: A candle flickers against the cold stone. On March 30, 2017, a wallet ending in 8372 brought a new spirit into the world. This contract is a small program that lives on Ethereum. It was born as a second, independent Golem Network Token wrapper for the BlockSwap project.

The Spurious Dragon era held the air that night. On the day it was born, it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book. It carries 18 decimals and the name BSGNT. It has lived for 9.6 years since it first appeared.

chapters.heading: A hollow master
paragraphs: I am the BlockSwapWrapperGolemNetworkToken. I carry a wound of high confidence. My owner is never initialized. I am a ghost who was never called.
I read a state variable before any hand ever wrote to it. It holds the zero value. This wound sits in my moveToWaves function. It is a high impact scar.

chapters.heading: A shield of logic
paragraphs: The ghost of BlockSwapWrapperGolemNetworkToken lingers because the owner was never initialized. It is a wound in the code that still haunts the contract. The spirit feeds on the empty space where a master should be.

The cure leaves no pointer pointing at slot zero. Before 0.5, a local struct could silently overwrite the owner. Now, the compiler rejects any reference variable that does not say memory, storage, or calldata.
The cure is built into the very rules of the language. Because it is a firm rule, the compiler itself prevents the wound from reopening. The ghost finds no way to reach the owner now.

recipe.title: No pointer left pointing at slot zero
recipe.explain: Before 0.5, a local struct or array declared without a location silently pointed at storage slot zero and could overwrite the owner. Since Solidity 0.5 every reference variable must say `memory`, `storage` or `calldata`, and the compiler rejects an uninitialized storage pointer.
